content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT PAGER — prod-gpu-pool-4: multiple containers entering CrashLoopBackOff. Reason: SIGSEGV in runtime attention kernel. High error rate on /generate route. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
ops-bot: summary: ~1200 5xxs/min, ~30% of requests returning 500s. Autoscaler triggering restarts. Affected nodes: gpu-04, gpu-07.

sylvie (oncall): I'm on it — joining. Anyone already looking at logs?

jordan (eng-runtime): I see repeating backtraces pointing to vllm/attn_kern.c:NULL deref. Also CUDA invalid memory errors interleaved. Quick paste of latest log:

```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] runtime: panic: SIGSEGV at 0x0
goroutine 1 [running]:
  vllm.attn_kern(0x7f8c..., 0x0)
  /srv/runtime/vllm/attn_kern.c:132
  ...
CUDA Error: CUDARuntimeError: invalid device pointer
Container restart reason: CrashLoopBackOff
```

kevin (sre): Notable: OOM events on gpu-07 preceding segfaults: kernel retries then segfault. Could be memory corruption.

sylvie (oncall): Immediate mitigation: scale down replicas of /generate to 30% to reduce concurrent kv_cache pressure. Can we route traffic to fallback model on cpu?

jordan (eng-runtime): Yes — we have model-embed-fallback (CPU) ready. I'll create a routing rule to divert 40% of traffic to fallback and 60% to host pool in us-west-2 where we have spare capacity.

jordan (eng-runtime): Command I'll run:
```
# switch route
redwood route update /generate --split 60:prod-gpu-pool-4,40:cpu-fallback
```

emily (cust-suc): Heads up — we have two customers on call (FinApps and Chatly) reporting degraded latency. Let me know ETA to reduce impact.

mike (support): Noted. Raising priority for both customers and opening incident tags in Zendesk.

kevin (sre): In parallel I'll cordon gpu-07 and drain it gracefully to stop further evictions.

ops-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: sylvie assigned; jordan assigned; kevin assigned. Incident severity: Sev2.

jordan (eng-runtime): Quick diagnostic: building and deploying a debug image with ASAN turned on to capture memory corruption traces. Pushing container to staging now. If we can reproduce a crash on a drained node with a single request we may get line-level trace.

sylvie (oncall): Good. Meanwhile roll restart of runtime service to clear any bad NVMap allocations? Or will that cause more restarts?

jordan (eng-runtime): Rolling restart helps but autoscaler will respawn into same binary. We need to either: (A) revert the last performance optimization (attention tiled prefetch) that touched attn_kern.c, or (B) hotfix with bounds checks. I recommend revert to stable build to stop immediate customer impact.

kevin (sre): Reverting sounds safest. Jordan, can you tag a build for rollback? I'll hold node cordon until rollback lands so we don't keep draining healthy nodes.

jordan (eng-runtime): Pushing rollback tag now:
```
# promote stable
image-promote runtime:v1.22.3 runtime:latest
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime -n prod
```

ops-bot: deploy started by jordan. Notifying oncall.

sylvie (oncall): Traffic split applied?

jordan (eng-runtime): Yes — split applied. CPU fallback taking ~40% load. Observability shows 5xx rate dropping from 30% -> 12% within 2m.

kevin (sre): gpu-07 drained and cordoned. No new OOMs on gpu-04 post-rollback yet. We're seeing fewer segfaults in recent logs.

mike (support): Communicating to FinApps and Chatly: workaround is active routing to fallback; new expected degraded P95 is ~450ms vs 180ms normal. Sending message now.

emily (cust-suc): Please add incident note: "short-term mitigation: route-split to CPU fallback, rollback runtime image to v1.22.3, drain gpu-07."

jordan (eng-runtime): We have an ASAN capture on staging that reproduces null deref. Root cause: under specific batch alignment the KV-cache pointer wasn't initialized when attention kernel called. Fix is trivial (init pointer before tiled loop) but we want thorough unit tests. I'll prepare patch and run canary on a single host before global rollout.

sylvie (oncall): Timeline?

jordan (eng-runtime): Patch, build, canary deploy ~45-60m if no surprises. Can cut a hotfix branch now.

kevin (sre): For rollback to be safe: ensure autoscaler cooldown increased to avoid immediate spikes. I'll set cooldown to 600s.

ops-bot: NOTE: Page silence requested at 11:00Z for follow-ups; escalation to Eng manager if customer impact persists.

mike (support): Support update sent. Customers acknowledged and asking for ETA; I shared the 60m estimate.

emily (cust-suc): Adding postmortem participants: jordan, kevin, sylvie, mike, emily. Will draft customer-facing summary after incident.

jordan (eng-runtime): Canary started on one host (gpu-09) with patched runtime. Monitoring telemetry: no segfaults so far across 1k requests. Latency stable. If stable for 10m, I'll promote hotfix to prod.

sylvie (oncall): Thanks all. I'll keep this thread open for handoff to next oncall at 11:30Z.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 10:55Z — error rate reduced to 2%, affected nodes stable, hotfix candidate canary healthy.

kevin (sre): Postmortem note: investigate memory fence ordering in attention kernel, add e2e with batch alignment fuzzing, add guard for kv_cache init.

jordan (eng-runtime): Preparing PR with tests. Will link here once ready.

mike (support): Closing high-priority customer tickets as mitigations confirmed; keeping them in watch mode.

sylvie (oncall): Handoff in 30m — I'll summarize in the runbook and escalate if any regression appears. Thanks team.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (provisional): 11:22Z — Hotfix promoted to prod, rollback and routing mitigations removed, error rates normalized. Follow-up: full postmortem and customer comms in #incidents-postmortem.
